stem: When did man first land on the Moon?
expl: On 20th July 1969 for the first time, man landed on the Moon. Three astronauts sent with the Apollo-11 mission to the Moon were Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins and Edwin Buzz Aldrin Junior. Among these astronauts, only Neil Armstrong and Edwin Aldrin walked on the surface of the Moon. On 16 July 1969, initiating its flight from Cape Kennedy Space Center, Florida (U.S.A.). Apollo-11 landed on the 'Sea of Tranquility' upon the Moon on 20 July 1969. On 21 July 1969 it started its return journey from the Moon towards the Earth and finally landed in the Pacific Ocean on 24 July, 1969.

The Area of large the black patch as seen from the Earth is called Lunar Mare or the “Sea of Tranquility” which is found on the large area of the Moon where the spacecraft Apollo-11 landed in 1969. Neil Armstrong was the first person to touch the surface of the Moon, followed by Edwin Aldrin Junior.

stem:
Assertion (A) : The same face of the Moon always faces the Earth.
Reason (R) : The Moon completes one rotation around its own axis in 23 and half days which is about the same time that it takes to orbit the Earth.

options.label: a
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: b
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

expl: The orbit of the Moon around the Earth is elliptical and tilted and therefore we can see only 59% of the Moon’s surface at a time. The Moon takes 27 days, 7 hours and 43 minutes to rotate on its axis. This is also the time of one revolution of the Moon around the Earth. This is the reason why we always see the same face of the Moon. Therefore, statement A is correct but reason R is incorrect.

stem: When any object is taken from the Earth to the Moon –

options.label: c
options.text: There is no change in its weight

expl: Weight of any object on any planet is equal to the product of its mass and gravitational acceleration. The Moon’s gravitational acceleration is 1/6th of Earth. Therefore, when an object is taken to the Moon its weight decreases to 1/6th of its original weight. Formula: Weight of Object = Mass × gravitational acceleration.

stem: A country by sending its ‘SELENE’ (Selenological and Engineering Explorer) in the orbit of the Moon became the first country in Asia. The country which achieved this fame is –
expl: SELENE is also known as ‘Kaguya’ is an orbiter spacecraft sent to the orbit of the moon by Japan on 14 September, 2007. It revolved around the moon for approximately 1 year and 10 months successfully and after that, it fell upon the surface of the Moon at Gill Crater voluntarily.
